deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of Euler's account (E598) of Lagrange's 'Recherches d'arithmétique' and its bearing on Euler's own older theory of the linear forms of prime divisors of p^2 ± n q^2.

§12 (Corollary 2). Classes of residues: Let a run over the residues mod 4n, coprime to 4n, that can occur as prime divisors of p^2 + n q^2. Let α run over the excluded residues. Euler recalls three facts he had proved earlier.
- The a-classes are closed under multiplication and powers, so they form a subgroup H of (Z/4nZ)^*.
- For a fixed α, the products aα, a'α, ... are again α's (a coset of H). Hence #α ≥ #a.
- The two classes have equal size, which Euler says 'can also easily be shown'.
He then adds the coset rules: the product of two α's (including a square α^2) lies in the a-class, and the product of three α's lies in the α-class. In modern terms, H is a subgroup of index 2, namely the kernel of the quadratic character χ_{-4n} (Kronecker symbol (-4n/·)), and the α's form the nontrivial coset.

§13 (Corollary 3). What remains: one must still show that the class 4ni+α contains every prime that cannot divide p^2+nq^2. Then every prime ≡ a (mod 4n) divides some number p^2+nq^2. This is Euler's linear-form version of quadratic reciprocity (the converse direction).

§14 (Problem IV). Prime divisors D of p^2 − n q^2, with gcd(p,q)=1 and p coprime to n.
- The condition gcd(p,n)=1 is imposed only to exclude the trivial divisors of n.
- If D divides p^2 − nq^2, then D also divides nq^2 − p^2. Multiplying by n gives n p^2 − r^2 with r = nq, so the inverted form n p^2 − q^2 is covered as well.
- As in the definite case (Lagrange), D = f r^2 + 2g rs + h s^2 with fh − g^2 = −n.
- Lagrange reduction allows |2g| ≤ |f| and |2g| ≤ |h|. Then |fh| ≥ 4g^2, so fh − g^2 = −n forces one coefficient to be negative. Write D = f r^2 + 2g rs − h s^2 with fh + g^2 = n.
- Then fh ≥ 4g^2 gives 5g^2 ≤ n, i.e. g ≤ √(n/5). So only finitely many, and few, reduced forms remain.
- Finally Df = f^2 r^2 + 2fg rs − fh s^2 = (fr+gs)^2 − n s^2, which is of the original shape. The next page adds Dh = n r^2 − (gr − hs)^2.
The aim is to translate Lagrange's reduction theory into Euler's 4ni ± a description of the divisors.
errors: Euler writes strict inequalities 2g<f, 2g<h, fh>4gg and 5gg<n. Lagrange's reduction only guarantees |2g| ≤ |f|, |h| (equality is possible), so the bound should read g ≤ √(n/5). Minor.

'Quod autem multitudo vtrinque sit prorsus aequalis, id etiam facile demonstrari potest' is overstated. Exact equality amounts to the a-subgroup having index exactly 2. One must show it is a proper subgroup, i.e. that some admissible residue is never a divisor (nontriviality of the quadratic character mod 4n). This is not entirely trivial by the elementary means Euler had in mind.
Implicitly, D must be taken coprime to n (and odd) for the reduced-form representation and the residue-class description to hold. This is consistent with the stated hypotheses but not repeated.
The step 'D divides npp − nnqq' tacitly multiplies the expression by n. It is harmless, since D is coprime to n.

ideas.what: Admissible residues a mod 4n form a multiplicative subgroup; the excluded α form a coset; αα' lies in the a-class and αα'α'' lies in the α-class; both classes have equal size.
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of the quadratic (Kronecker) character χ_{-4n} on (Z/4nZ)^*, a subgroup of index 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E164 and related papers, 1740s-1750s; E552), systematized by Legendre and Gauss / Dirichlet characters
ideas.where_published: E164 'Theoremata circa divisores numerorum in hac forma paa±qbb contentorum'; E552 'Observationes circa divisionem quadratorum per numeros primos'

ideas.what: Reduction of the problem to showing that 4ni+α contains all non-divisor primes, so that every prime ≡ a (mod 4n) divides p^2+nq^2.
Reduced indefinite binary forms f r^2+2grs−hs^2 with fh+g^2=n, |2g| ≤ |f|,|h|, giving g ≤ √(n/5); and Df=(fr+gs)^2−ns^2.
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange reduction of indefinite binary quadratic forms; the bound on reduced forms

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an expository restatement of Lagrange's reduction theory (with the standard √(n/5) bound for indefinite forms) and of Euler's well-known index-2 subgroup structure of divisor classes and his formulation of quadratic reciprocity. All of this is documented and credited in the standard histories.
